I could not fully derive this, so the answer below is a best recollection rather than a verified result.

The width is at least 2, since $\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$ is not commutative. I recall results on commutative-submonoid factorizations of infinite transformation monoids suggesting that the full transformation monoid on a countably infinite set splits into a small finite number of commutative submonoids, with 3 the value I associate with it. I did not reconstruct the decomposition or the proof that two factors are insufficient, so treat 3 as unverified.

ANSWER: 3
